parse.title: Cognitive fatigue
parse.wikitext:
<onlyinclude>'''Cognitive fatigue''' (also called exhaustion, tiredness, lethargy, languidness, languor, lassitude, and listlessness) is medically recognized as a state usually associated with a weakening or depletion of one's mental resources.<ref name="DSM5GlossaryCognitiveFatigue">{{cite journal|title=Glossary of Technical Terms|journal=Diagnostic and statistical manual of mental disorders (5th ed.)|year=2013|pages=821|doi=10.1176/appi.books.9780890425596.GlossaryofTechnicalTerms}}</ref><ref name="MizunoTanaka2011">{{cite journal|last1=Mizuno|first1=Kei|last2=Tanaka|first2=Masaaki|last3=Yamaguti|first3=Kouzi|last4=Kajimoto|first4=Osami|last5=Kuratsune|first5=Hirohiko|last6=Watanabe|first6=Yasuyoshi|title=Mental fatigue caused by prolonged cognitive load associated with sympathetic hyperactivity|journal=Behavioral and Brain Functions|volume=7|issue=1|year=2011|pages=17|issn=1744-9081|doi=10.1186/1744-9081-7-17}}</ref> The intensity and duration of this effect typically depends on the substance consumed and its dosage. It can also be further exacerbated by various factors such as a lack of sleep<ref>Alhola, P., & Polo-Kantola, P. (2007). Sleep deprivation: Impact on cognitive performance. Neuropsychiatric disease and treatment. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC2656292/</ref> or food<ref name="KimKang2017">{{cite journal|last1=Kim|first1=Jin Young|last2=Kang|first2=Seung Wan|title=Relationships between Dietary Intake and Cognitive Function in Healthy Korean Children and Adolescents|journal=Journal of Lifestyle Medicine|volume=7|issue=1|year=2017|pages=10–17|issn=2234-8549|doi=10.15280/jlm.2017.7.1.10}}</ref>. These feelings of exhaustion involve a wide variety of symptoms which generally include some or all of the following effects: 
*[[Analysis depression]]
*[[Motivation depression]]
*[[Thought deceleration]]
*[[Memory suppression|Short term memory suppression]]
*[[Thought disorganization]]
*[[Language depression]]
*[[Creativity depression]]
Cognitive fatigue is most commonly induced under the influence of [[dosage#common|moderate]] [[dosage|dosages]] of [[antipsychotic]] compounds,<ref name="SeoMacPherson2010">{{cite journal|last1=Seo|first1=Rubo J.|last2=MacPherson|first2=Holly|last3=Young|first3=Allan H.|title=Atypical Antipsychotics and Other Therapeutic Options for Treatment of Resistant Major Depressive Disorder|journal=Pharmaceuticals|volume=3|issue=12|year=2010|pages=3522–3542|issn=1424-8247|doi=10.3390/ph3123522}}</ref><ref name="WittkampfArends2012">{{cite journal|last1=Wittkampf|first1=Laura Christina|last2=Arends|first2=Johannes|last3=Timmerman|first3=Leo|last4=Lancel|first4=Marike|title=A review of modafinil and armodafinil as add-on therapy in antipsychotic-treated patients with schizophrenia|journal=Therapeutic Advances in Psychopharmacology|volume=2|issue=3|year=2012|pages=115–125|issn=2045-1253|doi=10.1177/2045125312441815}}</ref> such as [[quetiapine]], [[haloperidol]], and [[risperidone]]. However, it can also occur during the [[withdrawal]] symptoms of many [[depressant|depressants]],<ref name="ChaudhuriBehan2000">{{cite journal|last1=Chaudhuri|first1=Abhijit|last2=Behan|first2=Peter O|title=Fatigue and basal ganglia|journal=Journal of the Neurological Sciences|volume=179|issue=1-2|year=2000|pages=34–42|issn=0022510X|doi=10.1016/S0022-510X(00)00411-1}}</ref> and during the [[duration#offset|offset]] of many [[stimulant|stimulants]]<ref name="LagoKosten1994">{{cite journal|last1=Lago|first1=Jesus A.|last2=Kosten|first2=Thomas R.|title=Stimulant withdrawal|journal=Addiction|volume=89|issue=11|year=1994|pages=1477–1481|issn=0965-2140|doi=10.1111/j.1360-0443.1994.tb03746.x}}</ref>.</onlyinclude>
